record.paper_title: Brane Supersymmetry Breaking and the Cosmological Constant: Open Problems
record.original_question: In non-BPS brane-world compactifications that try to absorb the brane vacuum energy into curvature of the transverse extra dimensions rather than four-dimensional spacetime, under what precise geometric and boundary-condition assumptions does a closed compactification manifold admit a global solution without reintroducing fine-tuning? In particular, when the brane tension changes because supersymmetry is broken on a codimension-2 brane, can the transverse geometry and warp factor adjust continuously enough to absorb that arbitrary tension, or do deficit-angle sum rules and other global constraints obstruct such solutions unless the model has at least two, and perhaps effectively codimension-3-or-higher, extra dimensions?

evidence.quote: The issue of boundary conditions: due to obstructions to finding a global solution for the background geometry, it has been argued [9] that the Rubakov-Shaposhnikov mechanism cannot be extended to models with a single extra dimension [10]. It will be argued that in order to avoid similar problems, at least two extra dimensions are needed.

As for the first problem, if we want to have a closed compactification manifold, we must actually impose boundary conditions on α(r) and g̃(r) both at r = ǫ and at large r. But there may be global obstructions to our ability to impose such boundary conditions.

Since only a discrete set of brane cosmological constants can be absorbed in the transverse curvature, there is no continuus "Rubakov–Shaposhnikov modulus" that can be adjusted to absorb this arbitrary brane tension.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a brane-world compactification of the form $M_4 \times K$, where $M_4$ is four-dimensional spacetime and $K$ is a compact internal manifold with one or more codimension-$\geq 2$ branes (defects) of arbitrary tension $T$ supported on submanifolds of $K$. Write the higher-dimensional metric in warped form
$$ds^2 = e^{2A(y)}\,\eta_{\mu\nu}\,dx^\mu dx^\nu + \tilde g_{mn}(y)\,dy^m dy^n,$$
with the warp factor $A$ and internal metric $\tilde g$ depending only on the transverse coordinates $y\in K$. The Einstein equations are sourced by a bulk cosmological constant (possibly arising from fluxes or a bulk supergravity sector) together with delta-function brane stress-energies of tension $T$. A "Rubakov–Shaposhnikov absorption" of the brane tension is a smooth one-parameter family of regular solutions $(\tilde g(y;T), A(y;T))$ on the closed manifold $K$ for which $M_4$ remains exactly Ricci-flat for a continuous range of $T$.

(a) For $K$ closed and one-dimensional (codimension 1), determine whether any global solution of the bulk Einstein equations with prescribed boundary/junction conditions at the brane loci can absorb a continuous range of brane tensions $T$ into the transverse curvature while keeping $M_4$ flat, or whether sum rules (integrated Einstein equations / Gauss–Bonnet-type identities on $K$) obstruct such solutions and force a fine-tuning between $T$ and the bulk parameters.

(b) For a codimension-2 brane embedded in a closed two-dimensional internal space $K$, with a conical deficit angle $\delta(T)$ generated by the brane tension, determine whether the global Gauss–Bonnet constraint
$$\int_K \tilde R\,\sqrt{\tilde g}\,d^2y + \sum_i \delta_i(T_i) = 4\pi\chi(K),$$
together with regularity of $\tilde g$ and $A$ at all brane positions and away from them, allows a continuous family of solutions absorbing arbitrary tension $T$, or whether only a discrete set of tensions is compatible with closure of $K$ (so that no continuous modulus exists to absorb a generic supersymmetry-breaking tension shift).

(c) Determine the minimal codimension (in particular whether codimension $\geq 3$ is required) of the transverse space for which a continuous absorption modulus exists, allowing arbitrary brane tension to be absorbed into the internal geometry without reintroducing fine-tuning of the four-dimensional cosmological constant.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether transverse curvature can absorb brane tension in a self-tuning way—without fine-tuning of the four-dimensional cosmological constant—remains an active and unresolved problem. Codimension-1 self-tuning proposals are known to suffer from global obstructions / hidden fine-tunings, and while codimension-2 (6D supergravity) constructions have been studied extensively (e.g., "accidental SUSY" and related works), it is still open whether bulk supersymmetry guarantees stability and whether a continuous absorption modulus exists; the issue of deficit-angle sum rules forcing a discrete spectrum of admissible tensions is widely acknowledged.

status_evidence.title: Accidental SUSY: Enhanced Bulk Supersymmetry from Brane Back-reaction
status_evidence.snippet: Studies codimension-two branes in 6D gauged chiral supergravity and how brane tension is absorbed into transverse curvature via deficit angles.
status_evidence.claim: Codimension-2 absorption of brane tension via deficit angles is an active research direction, with stability of the self-tuning solution unresolved.

status_evidence.title: An Update on Brane Supersymmetry Breaking
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews ongoing open issues in brane supersymmetry breaking and the resulting runaway/cosmological-constant problem.
status_evidence.claim: The cosmological-constant absorption problem in brane-SUSY-breaking models is still discussed as open.

status_evidence.title: Codimension-two Branes overview
status_evidence.snippet: Deficit-angle sum rules constrain tensions of codimension-2 branes on compact transverse spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Global topological constraints (Gauss–Bonnet) restrict admissible brane tensions, supporting the conjectured obstruction.
